paper_metadata.title: Quantum computing for multidimensional option pricing: End-to-end pipeline

experiments.description: Quantum and classical estimation of cosine-series coefficients for the calibrated AXA NIG marginal density, comparing CMC versus QAMC/QAE on a 1D density-recovery task.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Accelerated Monte Carlo for cosine-series coefficient estimation using modified Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A 1D discretization of the marginal density on J = 2^n = 25 points is loaded into amplitudes; cosine basis functions gamma_k are estimated via controlled rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate cosine coefficients a_k = E[gamma_k(X)] for the AXA marginal density and reconstruct f(x) and F(x) from the truncated cosine series.

problem_instance.description: AXA calibrated NIG marginal density recovery from market option data.

dataset_specification.description: AXA European call/put quotes as of 24/12/2024; 1-year expiry (19/12/2025) used in the displayed experiment; calibrated NIG parameters alpha=5.24, beta=-3.26, delta=0.18, lambda=5e-7; spot price 33.8 EUR.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Mid-prices from bid-ask quotes; arbitrage sanity checks; NIG calibration; cosine-series truncation for density reconstruction.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each estimation repeated 25 times; errors compared against a classically computed Riemann quadrature reference; average error and 90% confidence intervals reported.

implementation_details.framework_version: myQLM 1.12.2; Python 3.10; NEASQC: Financial Applications Library 2024
implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Riemann quadrature for reference values
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute reference cosine coefficients via classical Riemann quadrature; use calibrated NIG density.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare coefficient errors and density/distribution reconstructions; compute averages and confidence intervals.

results.unit: normalized price error (spot fraction; approximately 21 basis points max)
normalized price error (spot fraction; approximately 10 basis points around ATM)
quadratic improvement over classical Monte Carlo; O(1/epsilon) vs O(1/epsilon^2)

speedup_claims.conditions: for cosine-series coefficient estimation via QAE/QAMC under the stated oracle model
speedup_claims.caveats: Empirical plots show the expected scaling; exact query counts for this experiment are not stated in the text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(b_i-a_i) K_i^2 / epsilon_i * log(K_i / rho_i)) per marginal reconstruction, as stated in Theorem 3.4
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/epsilon^2) Monte Carlo scaling for coefficient estimation

experiments.description: Quantum and classical pricing of a 2-asset spread call option under a Gaussian copula, comparing joint and independent QAMC formulations against CMC.

algorithm.variant: QAMC/QAE for multidimensional option pricing, joint formulation and independent formulation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-asset joint density is discretized on J = 2^n = 8 points per dimension; the joint density or independent-marginal adjusted payoff is loaded into amplitudes with one ancilla qubit for QAE.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the discounted spread option price V(T,K) = e^{-rT} E[max(S1(T)-S2(T)-K, 0)] under a Gaussian copula joint distribution built from calibrated NIG marginals.

problem_instance.description: Spread 1-year expiry call option on AXA and Michelin.

dataset_specification.description: AXA and Michelin market option quotes as of 24/12/2024; calibrated NIG marginals from the paper; Gaussian copula correlation matrix [[1,-0.25],[-0.25,1]].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Calibrated NIG marginals; cosine-series density reconstruction with K=27 computed classically to isolate final pricing error; Gaussian copula coupling.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: CMC versus QAMC comparison; both joint and independent QAMC formulations; repeated 25 times; average error and 90% confidence intervals reported against a classical Riemann-sum reference price.

implementation_details.framework_version: myQLM 1.12.2; Python 3.10; NEASQC: Financial Applications Library 2024
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Use calibrated NIG marginals and Gaussian copula; compute reference price classically.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare convergence of CMC, QAMC joint, and QAMC independent estimators.

results.uncertainty: 90% confidence intervals reported; exact numeric values not stated in text

results.unit: QAMC converges as O(1/epsilon) versus CMC O(1/epsilon^2)

experiments.description: Quantum and classical pricing of a 3-asset arithmetic basket call under a Gaussian copula, comparing joint and independent QAMC formulations against CMC.

algorithm.variant: QAMC/QAE for multidimensional option pricing, joint formulation and independent formulation
